prerequisites: Seeded shared work lab openlaw-docs-41255c61-work built from 3fa407e3; Daniel Okafor (Administrator) signs in with a password in an isolated browser context; Nadia Haddad is the second legal session for restricted-record fixtures.
Jonas Weber (Business User) signs in to the Portal with a fresh magic link from the lab Mailpit.

Per-role fixture from the walkthrough: an Advisory Matter with an open child, a Confidential child created by the other legal account, a linked NDA Contract, a Task, a future Key date and Jonas Weber on the team.
scenarios.expected: The selected Status retains its immutable open/closed Category and lifecycle changes persist. An archived Matter cannot be edited through ordinary controls; Contributor restrictions remain clear.
scenarios.actual: 8 recorded browser steps passed for this role (Daniel Okafor). Fixture M-126 had open child M-127, Confidential child M-128 created by Nadia Haddad, linked C-144, a Task, a future Key date and Jonas Weber on the team. The pill showed the exact Status and the Status strip showed Open, In progress, Waiting and Closed; the Open group Move to menu offered Open and On hold, and On hold saved at once with no dialog; With external counsel under Waiting also saved at once, stayed in the open Category and kept Opened with no Closed date. Closed > Closed opened the close dialog: Close matter stayed disabled without a Closing note, the note kept 2,000 of 2,100 typed characters, Open child Matters listed M-127 and "Restricted Matter" without the private child identity; Cancel kept the Status. Close matter set the Closed date (Overview showed a date), History showed the Closing note, the child stayed open, the Contract stayed Draft, the Task stayed not done, the Key date stayed and Next deadline became null; the default list omitted the Matter. The closed Matter still saved a Description and a Task, and Filter > Show closed listed it. In progress > In progress opened "Reopen …? The Matter returns to active surfaces. Its original opened date is preserved."; Cancel kept it closed; Reopen matter cleared Closed (Overview "Still open"), kept Opened, restored the Key date as Next deadline, and History kept every transition. Matter actions > Archive opened "The matter leaves the default list. Its history and M-number are kept."; Cancel changed nothing; Archive kept M-126 and History, showed the Status strip without Move to menus, removed the Description editor, refused direct writes with 409 "This matter is archived. Restore it before editing.", and left the child and Contract unarchived. For the closed archived Matter, Show archived alone did not list it and Show archived with Show closed did; Restore Cancel kept it archived; Restore made it editable (Description saved) and kept it closed. Jonas Weber saw the Status in the Portal with no lifecycle controls, the staff route sent him to /portal, and his Status, archive and restore writes answered 403.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical reviewer; not a human user study and not the feature owner approval.

The work lab is shared with other DOC-029 agents. A private lab could not be created (Docker address pools exhausted), so setup-r1.mjs added DOC-029-named Fields, two Matter types and three Matter templates; no existing setting changed, and teardown-r1.mjs archived them after the runs (moving the DOC-029 walkthrough Matters to the Other type). Only records named DOC-029 matters were created.

Fixture records and some state changes (closing before archive, archiving the work Matter, a person leaving the team) were set up through the lab API and are labelled Fixture in walkthrough-r1.json; the article procedures credited here used the browser controls.

In the full run, five legal_team_member steps of matter-status-and-archive timed out waiting for the Matter header to render; an immediate rerun passed every step and replaced them. The cause was not reproduced and is recorded in walkthrough-r1.json harnessNotes.
The seeded Statuses were used as they are; no Status was renamed, so the renamed-label example in the article was checked only through the group placement of seeded open Statuses under Waiting.
Help discovery, themes, keyboard operation and zoom were not rechecked in this round.

compatibilityReview.summary: From 3fa407e3 to 067c1646 (DOC-030, set compat): I read the diff of matter-record.tsx, matters/routes.ts, the new matters/service.ts, matters.tsx and lib/activity.ts. The Status strip, close and reopen dialogs, Opened and Closed facts, archive and restore actions and the Show closed and Show archived filters did not change; the lifecycle rules moved into the service unchanged. I replayed the DOC-029 V-C23 script for both roles on lab compatcmp built from 067c1646; all 16 steps passed (the Legal Team Member after two load-related page waits, rerun with no script change). Earlier review, DOC-029 round 3 compatibility reviewer (3fa407e3 to 432dba3a): From 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38, round 2 (DOC-029r2 compatibility reviewer (matters)) found the article compatible: I inspected the 3fa407e3..57e77e38 app diff and found no change to the Status strip, close, reopen, archive, restore or Matters filters; the changes are archived-person styling, sign-in branding, first-run and Settings list rows. I replayed the round 1 V-C23 walkthrough on the work2 lab as Administrator and Legal Team Member, and all 16 steps passed. From 57e77e38 to 432dba3a, round 3 found only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test changed. The wizard now goes to /auth/two-factor/enroll after it saves a policy that requires two-factor authentication. The article makes no statement about the setup wizard Authentication step or two-factor enrollment. The change touches only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test, so no statement in the article can become wrong.
